environmentalPersistence: Low — degraded by cytokinin oxidase (CKX) rapidly in plant tissue and soil

lowDose.description: Anti-senescence effects — maintains chlorophyll, promotes cell division and branching, delays leaf aging, promotes bud break, enhances sink strength. Leaves stay green longer; lateral buds activated.

highDose.description: Excessive cell division leads to callus-like growth, abnormal leaf morphology, epinasty, chlorosis from impaired chloroplast development at extreme doses. Abnormal meristematic proliferation.

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Mildly negative (promotes branching over height) at low dose; moderate at high dose from abnormal proliferation
morphologicalEffects.leafSize: Mildly increased at low dose; abnormal at high dose
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Mild at low dose (normal bushy growth); moderate epinasty at high dose
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Reduced at low dose (anti-senescence); mild at high dose
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strongly reduced at low dose (stay-green effect); moderate at high dose
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Strongly reduced at low dose; mild at high dose
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Mildly inhibited at both doses — cytokinins favor shoot over root
morphologicalEffects.branching: Strongly increased at low dose — lateral bud break is a primary cytokinin effect
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Old leaves benefit most from anti-senescence at low dose; new growth abnormal at high dose

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Opposite at low dose (maintains chlorophyll — anti-senescence); moderate at high dose
physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Maintained and extended at low dose; disrupted at high dose
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Maintained at low dose; mildly reduced at high dose

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Reduced at low dose (anti-senescence antioxidant effect); mild at high dose
molecularEffects.lipidPeroxidation: Reduced at low dose; mild at high dose

microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Near-normal — some PGPR produce cytokinins; exogenous CK can affect root exudate composition mildly

firstSymptoms: bud break and branching at low dose
lateSymptoms: maintained greenness and extended leaf life at low dose
callus-like proliferation at extreme high dose

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Low dose: maintained green on older leaves (anti-senescence). High dose: pale green, distorted leaves
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Old leaves (anti-senescence effect at low dose); apical meristem (branching)
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Distributed through branching pattern at low dose; distorted new growth at high dose
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Bushy, branched, green-maintained at low dose — very distinctive positive visual. Distorted at high dose.
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Low-moderate — BAP-riboside and zeatin signature; low compared to stress chemicals
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Good — normal growth pattern resumes after exposure ends

synergies.synergyNote: Cytokinin + N is a natural synergy — N availability signals cytokinin production in roots; together they maximize leaf area and photosynthetic capacity
synergies.antagonismNote: Cytokinin directly opposes ethylene-driven senescence (why CK keeps leaves green) and ABA-driven dormancy. This is the most educationally important antagonism in plant hormone biology.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Endogenous plant hormone — synthesized primarily in root tips; commercial BAP used in tissue culture and floriculture
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Tissue culture (essential for shoot multiplication); delays post-harvest yellowing in broccoli and leafy greens; promotes branching in ornamental plants
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Very low — no significant human health risk at horticultural concentrations
educationalContext.climateLink: Cytokinin signaling links root nitrogen sensing to shoot growth — relevant to understanding how plants integrate soil nutrient and climate signals
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — tissue culture laboratories; commercial spray products for ornamentals
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Why cut broccoli turns yellow in the fridge — cytokinin depletion after harvest. Spraying with cytokinins keeps it green. A direct connection between plant hormones and everyday food storage.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Food shelf life, sustainable horticulture, tissue culture for conservation of endangered plants
